meta.title: EasyLegal — Production Infrastructure Map
meta.subtitle: Dokploy + Traefik, 3 split compose deployments, 1 shared database

views.label: Public visitor request
views.note: Cloudflare terminates DNS/CDN, Traefik routes by Host() to the Next.js public sites.

views.label: Admin & data tooling
views.note: All internal tools are on a separate Dokploy compose deployment, routed by subdomain/path.

views.label: Shared state & external services
views.note: Postgres is a Dokploy-managed resource outside any compose file; MinIO backs uploads/images.

cards.title: Three Split Deployments
items: Public sites and internal infra are separate Dokploy compose apps so one push doesn't redeploy the other
easylegal.id (app-id) is a third, temporary-domain compose deployment
All three share one external `easylegal` Docker network

cards.title: Shared Database, Not In Compose
items: Postgres is a Dokploy-managed "Database" resource, reached via dokploy-network by container name
admin-api, PostgREST, Adminer, and both Next.js apps all read/write the same instance
No compose file defines its own postgres: service

cards.title: Edge & Access Notes (not all drawn as lines)
items: Cloudflare sits in front of Traefik for DNS/CDN and forwards real client IPs
Adminer also holds its own direct DATABASE_URL to Postgres behind Traefik basic auth — full read/write, treat as high-risk
Both Next.js apps (public_sites) also carry their own DATABASE_URL and MINIO_* env vars, not only via admin-api
MinIO is additionally exposed straight through Traefik at cdn.my.id / cdn-console.my.id, not only via admin-api
easylegal.my.id has a Cloudflare-level redirect to biz.id that must stay in sync with Traefik rules
